statement: For each a in {1,3}, there exists an integer N_a such that c_{6,(0,a)}(n)>0 for every integer n>=N_a, with c_{6,(0,a)} normalized and interpreted as in problem.md. Equivalently, each of the two Gerber--Norton e=6 charged-core coefficient sequences has only finitely many zero coefficients. This does not assert an effective value of N_a and does not settle positivity in every degree.
contribution: The result is a strict finite-exception refinement of the unresolved all-degree claim. It combines an exact level-rank identification with shifted rank-five A_5 cosets, an all-prime local-universality proof reduced to two explicit parity cosets for each charge, and Chan--Oh Theorem 4.9(1) to obtain global representation for all sufficiently large targets. The frozen Gerber--Norton source states only finite computational support; no priority assertion is made.
